summary: Red team of the accepted library audit AUDIT-06 (four Tau Ceti roadmaps: OneParameterSemigroups, FuchsianOrbifolds, OptimalTransport and AnalyticNumberTheory). Every one of the 702 cited declarations exists at the pinned commits. 69 findings: 3 high, 28 medium, 38 low. The three high ones: FuchsianOrbifolds layer 2 and the roadmap summary say no covolume of a Fuchsian group exists, although Mathlib's MeasureTheory.covolume (FundamentalDomain.lean:679), with Tau Ceti's PSL(2, R) measurability and invariance instances, is exactly it; FuchsianOrbifolds layer 3 cites strictPeriods_eq_zmultiples_strictWidthInfty and strictWidthInfty_pos as literally giving the full cusp stabilizer wℤ, but strictPeriods is only the lattice of unipotent translations and the positivity lemma assumes an arithmetic group; and AnalyticNumberTheory AN.3 cites three private Perron-file declarations for contour-shift bookkeeping and says the ingredients exist only for the Perron kernel, although Tau Ceti's completed ContourIntegration roadmap proves the residue theorem and the argument principle for closed piecewise-C1 curves in star-shaped domains. The medium ones: library material marked absent or uncredited (the Borel structure and evaluation maps on C(X, Y), BV curves and their variation measures, the atom inequality HasLaw.measure_singleton_le, the Hecke-character ideal weights with their Euler products and the ray class group, Mathlib's continuation of the residue-class von Mangoldt L-series to Re s ≥ 1, the Kolmogorov decomposition RKHS.OfKernel, the Hausdorff and second-countable coarse quotient, the positive-definite kernel predicate), targets marked tauceti or built that are partial (the extended-cost c-transform, the bounded-below lower-semicontinuity theorem, the acceptance examples of OneParameterSemigroups part C), Mathlib's cusp API being for GL(2, R) subgroups while the roadmap's Fuchsian groups are PSL(2, R) subgroups, private citations, missing or overstated duplicate records, and summaries that misstate what is built or missing.

Only the application is missing: a rectangle boundary packaged as a piecewise-C1 closed curve and split into its sides, and horizontal and vertical bounds for zeta'/zeta times x^s/s.
